candidate_attacked: Build a polynomial-size noncommutative ABP whose monomials are exactly the satisfying assignments, then run polynomial-time noncommutative ABP identity testing.

family.name: PAIR_EQUALITY_CNF_F_k
family.formula: F_k = AND_i (x_i <-> y_i), represented by the two implications per pair and padded to 3-CNF when required.
family.satisfying_assignments: Exactly the 2^k assignments with x-vector equal to y-vector.

solution_word_polynomial.meaning: Every monomial is one satisfying assignment, with variables ordered x_1...x_k,y_1...y_k.

theorem.name: PAIR_EQUALITY_SOLUTION_WORD_POLYNOMIAL_REQUIRES_EXPONENTIAL_NONCOMMUTATIVE_ABP_WIDTH_V0_5
theorem.statement: Every noncommutative single-source/single-sink algebraic branching program computing S_k has width at least 2^k at the degree-k cut, and hence size at least 2^k.
proof: Form Nisan's degree-k coefficient matrix M_k whose rows are degree-k x-prefix words and columns are degree-k y-suffix words.
The coefficient of prefix(a) suffix(b) in S_k is 1 iff a=b and 0 otherwise.
Therefore the 2^k by 2^k submatrix indexed by these prefixes and suffixes is exactly I_{2^k}.
Nisan's noncommutative ABP rank characterization lower-bounds ABP width at that cut by rank(M_k), so width >=2^k and total ABP size is exponential.
theorem.source_anchor: Noam Nisan, Lower Bounds for Non-Commutative Computation, STOC 1991; later expositions state the minimum noncommutative ABP width via these coefficient-matrix ranks.

interpretation.killed_route: Explicitly constructing the exact satisfying-assignment word polynomial as a polynomial-size noncommutative ABP and then using ABP-PIT.
interpretation.strength: The obstruction already occurs on a very easy equality/2-SAT family; it is representation complexity of the full solution polynomial, not SAT hardness of the family.
interpretation.important_nonclaim: This does not rule out a smaller decision-only noncommutative object that is nonzero iff F is satisfiable but does not encode every satisfying assignment monomial separately.
